newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metal Man says outlook uncertain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metal Man says outlook uncertain.

text.p: Metal Manufactures Ltd said on Wednesday that signs of a recovery in some parts of the economy had not yet flowed through to the group's results and the timing of a broad-based recovery was still uncertain.

"Early signs of a recovery in some sectors of the Australian economy had not yet flowed through to group results and the timing of a broadly based recovery is still uncertain," Metal Manufactures said in its annual results statement.
Earlier, Metal Manufactures reported annual net profit fell 17.8 percent to A$38.50 million. Pre-abnormals net profit fell 4.9 percent to A$41.2 million.
There was a A$4.2 million restructuring charge from the cables business.
Earnings per share fell to 17.7 cents from 22.1 cents and a seven cents per share dividend was set, down from 10 cents in 1995.

"While sales have been maintained near our 1995 levels, the subdued domestic market has impacted on margins and profitability," Metal Manufactures Managing Director Glenn Dudley said in the statement.

"A number of businesses performed well during the year but exposure to under performing sectors of the economy, most notably housing and construction, adversely impacted some areas particularly the Energy Cables and Vinidex plastic pipe
"The Group is well positioned to take advantage of new investment opportunities with a strong operating cash flow in 1996 reducing gearing to 33 percent."
Shares in Metal Manufactures, about 61.5 percent owned by BICC Plc, were untraded at 10.50 a.m. (2350 GMT), having closed unchanged at A$3.17 on Tuesday.
